record.what_it_does: Multichannel helpdesk and live chat software with ticketing, call center and knowledge base.
record.auth_notes: The REST API v3 uses a per-account API key sent in the `apikey` header. Keys are created in the agent panel under Configuration > System > API, with per-key permissions. The key is tied to a customer-specific domain (<account>.ladesk.com or a custom domain). API v1 and v3 keys are separate. The built-in MCP endpoint supports OAuth 2.1 with PKCE or a bearer token, but I found no OAuth for the REST API itself. A multi-user toolkit would have each user supply their domain and API key.
record.access_notes: There is no free plan, only a 30-day no-card trial. After that a paid plan is needed. The pricing page lists API keys per plan: Starter 1, Team 5, Business 10, Enterprise unlimited. Keys are self-serve in the account. External MCP connections are listed for Business and Enterprise.
record.api_breadth_notes: API v3 covers tickets, messages, customers, contacts, agents, departments, companies, knowledge base, calls, tags and more. I did not count the operations. The reference is served per account at /docs/api/v3, inside the admin panel.
record.mcp_notes: Each account has its own endpoint at https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp, using Streamable HTTP. Auth is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE or a bearer token. It is described as an early preview. A separate open-source server is at github.com/qualityunit/liveagent-mcp-server, published by QualityUnit.
record.blocker_notes: The API needs a paid plan after the 30-day trial. Credentials are per-account and per-domain, so users must enter their own subdomain and API key. The full API reference is only visible inside a logged-in account.

evidence.quote: you can use the swagger (OpenAPI) API descriptor which can be found at the very top of the API v3 documentation.

record.needs_human: The v3 docs are behind account login. The `apikey` header detail came from search-result summaries of support articles, not a page I opened. Please confirm it. Also confirm that webhooks exist (I believe they are set up as a "Call URL" action in rules), the 'no sandbox' finding, and which plans include MCP.
